title: Matching fragment cards with rolling and reserve trays
method:
A paper-card writer keeps four positions in its register (single word, line entry, line body and line exit) and separate registers for opening and ordinary lines. Fit their weighted word-card counts, length distributions and EVA-basic glyph counts on certain paragraph lines in the public ZL practice training split. A line starts with a blank edge mark. Each new word takes the previous card's final glyph as its edge mark. The register looks up cards by position, opening status and edge mark, falling back to the position table for a lookup with fewer than 14 observations. Every register weight is multiplied by the same final-glyph factor, ((position count + 1)/(pooled count + 4)) to the power 0.8. The conditional card count is used to power 1 at an entry or exit and 0.67 in the body.

In the body, a four-slot rolling tray supplies a card with probability 0.56 and a thirteen-slot reserve tray with probability 0.29. Each tray renews one randomly chosen slot after a line. Cards are drawn with replacement from body-word counts in one randomly chosen bank of 24 consecutive public training folios, changing banks after each 35 ordinary lines. Opening lines use a separate pair of trays along the same sequence of banks, paced by the opening-line fraction in the training data. The draw within a tray weights each card by its opening-status and final-glyph weights and the compatibility of its initial glyph with the edge mark. Full-word shapes are on the cards from the start. A card's selection does not depend on whether it was written earlier. Another 0.09 of body draws come from the current bank's full register and the remaining 0.06 from the pooled register. Starts and exits use the pooled register.

A rolling-tray draw switches one fragment with probability 0.88. A register draw in the body switches one with probability 0.40. The reserve tray retains the card intact. A fragment is one glyph in EVA-basic. The writer shuffles the inner slots and also considers the final slot with probability 0.14. At the first available switch, it selects an alternate glyph weighted by the 0.8 power of public counts conditioned on the two surrounding glyphs, or by the final-glyph table for the preceding glyph and position when switching an ending. Whole words, meaning categories, folio identifiers, and Currier and section labels play no role in choosing when a tray is replenished. The counts may be implemented with weighted slips or indexed dice tables. No glyph is singled out in any rule.

Practice-only exploration compared more diffuse and more concentrated trays at the same primary seed. The submitted text is seed 408, comprising 2,200 ordinary lines and 2,200 opening lines. Exact in-line four-grams were screened against the scorer's public copy guard and a colliding line redrawn. There are 38,640 words and no uncertainty marks. On the public practice split the specimen reproduced 14 of 19 facts. The long-word within-page reuse share was 0.278, and dependency on the line above by one-edit variants had an excess of 0.0134. The same fixed settings with seeds 409 and 410 gave reuse 0.271 and 0.284, and one-edit excess 0.0206 and 0.0200. The same seed with both trays disabled dropped reuse to 0.098. The interior paragraph-opener effect F-019 fell below threshold in seeds 409 and 410. The line cut packs the sampled pages next to one another in the synthetic text, so the F-011 result alone does not establish similarity at the same physical distance across a full book.
